notes: Under A159 (Fable audit, card L3) a law effect recorded with no money (a right or an eligibility lost or granted) is felt like a tenth of a month's pay. The size is one constant, NON_MONEY_FELT_SIZE in src/simulation/law-exposure.ts, marked PLACEHOLDER, and read through lawExposureFeltSize by both readers: the official views a person forms (living-world/official-views.ts) and whether they band together against the law (living-world/law-interest-groups.ts).

A tenth of a month's pay is where a money loss starts to count toward a group and where a view feels it fully; it was chosen so a lost right is never smaller than the smallest money loss that matters. It is a placeholder, not a measured equivalence.
Every non-money effect is the same size today. A lost vote, a lost license and a lost benefit eligibility likely differ by a large factor, and by the person's circumstances.
question: How large, in money or as a share of income, does a person feel the loss of a right or an eligibility under a law (a benefit they no longer qualify for, a license, a vote, a protection), and how does that size vary by what was lost and by the person's income?

sourcesChecked.source: Tversky and Kahneman, Loss Aversion in Riskless Choice, Quarterly Journal of Economics, 1991
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Losses weigh about twice equal gains; it gives no money size for a lost right or eligibility.

sourcesChecked.source: Sommers et al., Medicaid Work Requirements: Results from the First Year in Arkansas, New England Journal of Medicine, 2019
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: How many people lost coverage and what followed for them; it does not value the loss or measure how strongly they reacted against the law.

title: How big a lost right or eligibility feels
usableAnswer: Willingness-to-pay or willingness-to-accept figures, or survey reaction strengths, for losing named eligibilities and rights, as a share of monthly income by income band, so NON_MONEY_FELT_SIZE can become a table by kind of loss.
whyItMatters: A law that strips an eligibility moves no money on the record, so without a size the people it hurts would never blame its sponsors or organize against it, and a player who passes such a law would face no response.
